clue.text: Eruption, earth tremors and particles of lava

indicators.note: tremors shake the ground, so the letters of the word before are shaken into a new order

parts.note: ash is made of fine fragments thrown out by a volcano

explanation.surface: A volcano erupts, the ground shakes and bits of lava fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tremors' shakes EARTH into HEATR; the volcanic surface makes 'Eruption' look like lava, but it is a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash of red spots breaking out on the skin is called an eruption in medical language.

definitions.meaning: to attack harshly in words, as a reviewer might pan a play
in bridge and whist, winning every trick is a grand one of these

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for harsh criticism, and the bridge term for taking all (or all but one) of the tricks.

indicators.note: only the interior of the robot word is kept, its outer letters trimmed away

parts.note: an automaton is a self-operating machine, a robot

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what you would find if you opened up a robot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside of' strips AU from the front and N from the end of AUTOMATON. The definition is the answer to 23 across: salad that rabbits might eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A red salad fruit is a typical item in the leafy fare of 23, the salad a rabbit would nibble.

clue.text: 23 for Grant? Cut up a quarter

parts.note: to grant permission is to let

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
east is one of the four quarters of the compass, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A salad for someone called Grant, with a quarter of it chopped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CUT into TUC. 'Grant' looks like a man's name, but is the verb meaning allow.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy green salad plant, the classic food of the rabbit in 23.

indicators.note: mashed vegetables are broken up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
the answer to 22 across is used as letters

explanation.surface: Sausage with a second helping of mashed root vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mashed' mixes MO and the answer to 22 across. A banger is British slang both for a sausage, which the surface suggests, and for an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a banger is a battered old automobile, the sense needed here.

clue.text: Girl I'd brought up, dreadful liar, is different

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means these words are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a miss is a young woman or girl
I'd is written as the letters ID

indicators.note: a dreadful version is a badly mangled one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful liar of a girl who grew up quite unlike the rest of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns MISSID into DISSIM; 'dreadful' rearranges LIAR into ILAR. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are unlike one another are different; the two words are synonyms.

parts.note: post mortem means after death, here giving the death or end, with what follows placed after it
Paul is the setter, so Paul's is 'I have', shortened to I've

explanation.surface: Paul the setter wondering what follows after his death.
explanation.walkthrough: Latin 'post mortem' means 'after death', so the setter's own contraction is placed after the word for death. Paul is the setter, so 'Paul's' is first person. The definition is the salad of 23.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter leafy salad plant, one of the foods a rabbit eats in 23.

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of praise, as said to someone who has done well
a steak cooked through is the opposite of one barely cooked, the answer to 24 down

explanation.definitionFit: A cry of praise, and the steak term for meat cooked all the way through, not rare.

indicators.note: around means the first piece is wrapped about the second

parts.note: on and on means continually, giving ON twice
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something that keeps going round and round a single point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts I inside ON ON, as in going 'on and on'. The definition is the salad of 23.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent bulb sliced into salads, part of the rabbit fare named in 23.

clue.text: Particle categorically stopping short of nitrogen?

definitions.meaning: a category list runs from A to Z; stopping short of N, the symbol for nitrogen, it runs from A to M

explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of a chemical element, and 'A to M', an alphabet run that halts before N.

clue.text: Ruth and Sophia composed the origin of their work?

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of the names are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Two women writers, Ruth and Sophia, compose a joint work and claim credit for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges RUTH and SOPHIA together; 'and' is just a join. The surface makes 'composed' look like writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a book makes you its originator, so being the source of a work is this state.

clue.text: Greek poetess has curiously written about proxy love

indicators.note: written about means the scrambled letters are put round the next piece
curiously signals the letters of the short word are arranged oddly

parts.note: pp, per procurationem, is written when signing as a proxy for someone
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A Greek poetess composing verses about love conducted by proxy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' signals the anagram and 'written about' the container; pp, per pro, is what a secretary writes when signing on someone's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous lyric poet of ancient Lesbos, the best known woman poet of Greece.

clue.text: American case of policeman turned lunatic (bet lunatic arrested)

indicators.note: turned means the word for policeman is read backwards

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman

indicators.note: arrested means the scrambled letters are held inside the word for lunatic

parts.note: a kook is a crazy person

indicators.note: the second lunatic is a sign that the letters of the word bet are deranged

explanation.surface: A cop goes mad and has to be arrested after a crazy bet.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'lunatic' is a synonym and the second, inside the brackets, is an anagram signal; 'turned' reverses the policeman and 'arrested' holds the scrambled bet.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage this word means a wallet or handbag, a case for money.

parts.note: see you is texting shorthand CU, from the sounds of the letters
a Cumberland is a famous British sausage; with land left as land, sausage stands for the rest of that name

explanation.surface: A farewell, 'see you at Sausageland!', as if signing off from a theme park.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cumberland is a coiled British pork sausage: 'Sausage' replaces CUMBER in its name. The definition is the salad of 23.
explanation.definitionFit: A long green salad vegetable sliced into sandwiches, part of the rabbit fare of 23.

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: kernel-less means the central letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: the hickory is a nut tree

explanation.surface: A remark about a nut whose kernel has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kernel-less' takes the middle letter K out of HICKORY. The definition is the salad of 23; 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter salad leaf, one of the plants a rabbit might eat in 23.

clue.text: 23 (part two) — fix a huge amount for Italy

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly
tons means a huge amount
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Fixing a huge sum of money for Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part two' points to the second word of 23 only: food, not the rabbit kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbed tubes of pasta are an Italian food, the second word of 23.

clue.text: Early piece of advertising to avoid

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the promotion business
to elude is to avoid or escape

explanation.surface: An early example of advertising one would rather avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An introductory musical movement played first, before the main work.

indicators.note: rotten means decayed, so the letters are broken down and rearranged

explanation.surface: A scathing review of a bad book about the painter Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' rearranges BOOK ON DR. 'Turner' looks like J M W Turner, the painter; here it is the thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle you twist to open a door is literally something that turns.

clue.text: Defence for revolutionary, nothing but revolutionary

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: the second revolutionary means the letters of the next word turn over into a new order

explanation.surface: A fortress held for a revolutionary leader and nobody else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' the second time is the anagram signal, turning BUT into UBT; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small outlying fort built to defend a position, a defensive work.

clue.text: Cleaner figure halved for ease, it's said, good to enter

indicators.note: halved means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: a square is a geometrical figure

indicators.note: to enter means the letter goes inside the row of Es
it's said marks a phrase heard rather than read

parts.note: said aloud, this sounds like four letter Es

explanation.surface: Instructions for an easier figure, cut in half, with good input.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved' leaves SQU of SQUARE; 'for ease' 'it's said' sounds like 'four Es', EEEE, which G enters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber-bladed tool for wiping windows is a cleaning implement.

indicators.note: reportedly marks a word as heard spoken

parts.note: quarts are measures of liquid

explanation.surface: Someone reports the measurements of a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' makes QUARTS sound the same as the crystal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard crystalline mineral, varieties of which such as amethyst are cut as gems.

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a sound is picked up

parts.note: a metric carat weighs 0.2 grams

explanation.surface: A tiny weight being lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' has CARAT heard as the orange root. The definition is the salad of 23.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange root vegetable is the classic thing a cartoon rabbit munches, as in 23.

clue.text: Old man, fish and short man standing

parts.note: cod is a fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing means the word is read upwards

parts.note: Reg is short for Reginald, a man's name

explanation.surface: An old man standing with a fish and a short man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns REG into GER.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for an elderly man, often a grumpy or eccentric one.

parts.note: waffle is idle chatter, which Britons call rabbit, and also a batter dish, which is food: a two-word double definition clue for it

explanation.walkthrough: To 'rabbit' is British slang for chattering on, the same as to waffle; a waffle is also something to eat. The phrase therefore works as a clue to waffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive name for salad greens, and a two-part clue whose halves each mean waffle.

definitions.meaning: a dissolute man who chases women
a long-handled garden implement with teeth

explanation.definitionFit: Both a libertine man and the toothed garden implement for gathering leaves.

clue.text: Bottom? Then second to bottom's exceptional

indicators.note: the second letter is shifted to the bottom, which in a down answer is the end

parts.note: rear is the bottom or backside

explanation.surface: A remark about bottoms ranked second from last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second to bottom's' moves the second letter E of REAR to the end; 'Then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom found is uncommon, unusual, exceptional.

indicators.note: mid means the letters are taken from the middle of the phrase

explanation.surface: A compass point lying midway between south and north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid' picks the letters straddling the words in the middle of 'south or north'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickle on a rose stem is a sharp point.

indicators.note: sounds signals the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them, and a way is a route

explanation.surface: Someone asks which sounds are the best way forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' turns BEAT ROUTE into the vegetable. The definition is the salad of 23.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple root vegetable eaten in salads, part of the rabbit fare of 23.
